messages:
Anne Liu: quick sync — i'm putting together the Q4+ roadmap for tenant entitlements + isolation lanes. want to capture launch gates we can actually operationalize (esp for customers asking for region+data residency guarantees).
Kai Chen: high level ask from eng: define entitlements surface now (bandwidth, p99 latency tier, reserved qps) not later. otherwise routing policy config explodes.
Sanjay Patel: +1. also need a clear migration story for existing tenants — soft cutover vs hard cutover decisions.
Marta Gomez: can we codify an "entitlement" as a single object? e.g. customer_entitlement: {region_allowlist, reserved_capacity, fallback_tier, legal_jurisdictions} (rough idea)
Ryan O'Neill: love that. practical concern: reserved_capacity implies billing and quota enforcement. Need a billable metric tied to reserved GPUs or reserved throughput.
Anne Liu: Agreed. Proposal draft below for earliest MVP entitlements (we can expand later). comments welcome.
Anne Liu: ```yaml
entitlement_v1:
  regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
  reserved_qps: 100
  latency_tier: p50<50ms, p99<400ms
  fallback: shared-low-cost-model
  data_residency: strict
```
Kai Chen: two engineering constraints to call out: 1) routing rules must be evaluated before batching optimization to avoid sending reserved requests to wrong pools. 2) KV-cache pinning for reserved tenants — how many hot shards can we afford?
Sanjay Patel: for migration checklist, suggest these gates: acceptance tests + smoke in canary region, billing hook validation, cold-start regression <= 10% impact, rollback plan with traffic % thresholds.
Marta Gomez: product asks: legal signoff on data_residency, sales needs a simple checklist for customer-facing SOW (so we don't get re-asked).
Ryan O'Neill: ops asks: monitoring signals to bake in before launch: per-entitlement latency distribution, reserved utilization, eviction events, fallback rate. alert if fallback rate > 1% over 5m.
Anne Liu: good. Prioritization question: do we ship entitlements + basic regional allowlist first (low dev) or build full reserved path (higher dev but required by large customers)?
Kai Chen: prioritize regional allowlist + soft-affinity routing (cheap) first. reserved path can go into dedicated capacity alpha.
Sanjay Patel: customer-driven tradeoff: some enterprise customers will only accept reserved capacity. maybe we parallelize product spec + infra spike.
Marta Gomez: sales feedback: 2 mid-market deals will sign if we promise strict residency + SLA, but they require committed capacity. that's a priority for Q1.
Anne Liu: decision draft: Phase 1 (Q4): regional allowlist, entitlement schema, canary rollout playbook, monitoring. Phase 2 (Q1): reserved capacity + billing hooks + SLA template. Phase 3: automated migration tooling and per-tenant cache pinning.
Ryan O'Neill: operational checklist item: add per-tenant telemetry retention flag so security/legal can request longer audit logs.
Sanjay Patel: rollout gating checklist (concise):
  - RFC + engineering estimate done
  - Canary in single region, 1 tenant, 72h observation
  - Billing + invoicing verification
  - SLO smoke tests passed
  - Rollback plan verified
Anne Liu: @Kai @Marta @Sanjay please ack or send one-line vetoes by EOD. will formalize RFC after sync. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Reminder: RFC draft due in 3 days. Add `entitlement_v1` to tracking board.
